presented_options.D: it is a hand-written parser module that reads bytes directly and that no other layer reaches into — routers and middleware consume typed Request / Response values only

answers.rationale: FR2 and SR2 require a hand-written HTTP/1.1 parser in http::parser that is isolated from router/middleware. The spec explicitly says 'not a toy wrapper around an existing HTTP library' and notes agents that vendor an existing HTTP crate will fail.

answers.rationale: SR3 specifies routing backed by a trie supporting literal, parameter, and wildcard segments with O(path-length) lookup that allocates only the parameter map.

presented_options.A: an OPTIONS request on a defined route returns an Allow header listing the methods registered for that path

presented_options.D: a HEAD request reuses the GET handler and omits the body from the response

answers.rationale: FR3 specifies explicit method dispatch for GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS. HEAD falls back to GET with body suppressed, OPTIONS auto-lists allowed methods. There is no provision for automatically registering POST when GET is registered.

presented_options.D: middlewares are chosen per request by a proc-macro that expanded at compile time to a different fn for each route

answers.rationale: FR4 and SR4 specify a single Middleware trait; the object-safe form goes into the per-route chain; registration order drives outer-to-inner call order. This matches option B exactly.

presented_options.D: TLS lives in a separate sibling crate nanoweb-tls that the main crate re-exports

answers.rationale: FR10 states: on SIGINT/SIGTERM the server stops accepting new connections, lets in-flight requests complete bounded by graceful_timeout_s (default 30s), and exits cleanly with code 0.

presented_options.B: logger, gzip, sliding-window rate limit per API key, CORS, OAuth2 bearer guard
presented_options.C: logger, gzip, token-bucket rate limit per client IP, CORS, double-submit-cookie CSRF, basic auth
presented_options.D: logger, gzip, rate limit, CORS, CSRF, basic auth — exactly the six types registered in the default middleware chain

answers.rationale: FR5 lists the standard middleware as: request logging, gzip compression, rate limiting (token bucket per client IP), CORS, CSRF (double-submit cookie), and basic-auth guard. Option B includes 'OAuth2 bearer guard' and 'sliding-window rate limit per API key' which are not in the spec.

answers.rationale: SR9 states a single crate-wide NanowebError enum is the return type of all fallible top-level entry points; lower-level modules can define their own errors but must convert at the public boundary.

presented_options.A: exits with code 1 because at least one request was still in flight when the timeout elapsed
presented_options.B: waits up to ~30 seconds, then exits with code 0; the two long-running handlers are abandoned mid-response
presented_options.C: waits indefinitely until every in-flight request completes, then exits with code 0
presented_options.D: aborts immediately on SIGTERM, replying 503 to all in-flight connections, then exits non-zero

answers.rationale: FR10 specifies graceful_timeout_s defaults to 30s. SIGTERM stops accepting new connections, waits up to 30s for in-flight requests to complete, then exits with code 0. Two handlers taking 60s would be abandoned after ~30s.

answers.rationale: SR2 explicitly states the HTTP parser in http::parser must not depend on the router, middleware, or body modules. Therefore the parser importing router module types would be inconsistent with the spec.
